A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FixAgent, despite substantial changes to its architecture and presentation. All pages, tables and figures support comparison. v1 has no appendix; v2 includes readable Appendices A.1–A.4.

before.justification: Section V reports original FixAgent evaluations on Codeflaws, QuixBugs and ConDefects, including model comparisons and ablations.

after.justification: Section 4 reports original evaluations on four benchmarks, including Defects4J, agent and tool ablations, and comparisons across LLM backbones.

M1.justification: v1's localizer–repairer–revisitor pipeline, additional Crafter and best-patch feedback resampling become a three-level, seven-agent architecture. v2 adds retrieval, repository-file selection, summarization, slicing and static/dynamic tool use, with failure-triggered escalation and reverse-order refinement. Localization, repair and variable tracking remain recognizable, but Crafter is removed and coordination changes substantially.

E1.justification: v2 retains Codeflaws, QuixBugs and ConDefects and adds evaluation on 806 Defects4J bugs from 15 real-world Java projects. This extends coverage from competition and algorithm programs to repository-scale debugging involving cross-file dependencies; the programming-language coverage remains C, Java and Python.

E2.justification: Compared with v1 Table I, v2 Table 1 adds Recoder and ChatRepair to the retained QuixBugs comparisons, introduces Tbar and Repilot in the new Defects4J comparison, and removes Codex as an evaluated comparator. LLaMA2-70b and Claude-3.5-Sonnet join the LLM comparisons, alongside updated GPT and Gemini models. RewardRepair was already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: The default backbone changes from GPT-4-0125-preview to gpt-4o, and the three-attempt budget becomes five for FixAgent-Lite and twenty for full FixAgent and LLM baselines. Table 1 labels single-LLM baselines as using perfect FL, whereas v1 labels them as receiving no FL. v2 adds local-corpus retrieval during evaluation and dollar-cost measurement, moves the paired backbone comparison to ConDefects, and reports only plausible fixes there.

E4.justification: v1's four design-removal ablations on 300 Codeflaws bugs are replaced by cumulative agent configurations and retrieval/static-analysis/dynamic-analysis/testing-feedback ablations on Defects4J. Separate tracking and context-removal tests disappear. v2 also adds a fixed-bug overlap diagram and detailed Defects4J cases in Appendices A.1 and A.4, including a failed intermediate patch and its attempted refinement.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental replication counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Both estimate Codeflaws patch correctness using 100 sampled plausible patches. Changed patch-attempt limits are search budgets, not repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v1 Table I reports 2701 plausible Codeflaws fixes with 93% sampled correctness and 79 correct QuixBugs fixes; v2 Table 1 reports 3130, 95% and 80 for FixAgent-Lite. These concern changed methods, backbones and budgets, not controlled same-setting gains. v2 adds 197 correct Defects4J fixes and replaces the backbone/ablation results, while dropping ConDefects correctness counts. Its full-system plausible total is 286 in Table 1 but 291 in Tables 2 and 4 without an explained setting difference.

T1.justification: Neither version develops mathematical theory, proofs or formal guarantees. v1's sampling notation and v2's Algorithm 1 describe procedures; the newly cited cognitive debugging model provides conceptual motivation rather than mathematical development.

C1.justification: The end-to-end unified-debugging claim remains, but the central contribution shifts from rubber-ducking-inspired specialization, tracking and context construction to cognitive-model-based hierarchical coordination and adaptive handling of bug complexity. v2 foregrounds repository-scale repair and removes v1's claim that its high correctness rate could overcome patch overfitting.

C2.justification: v1 emphasizes context and variable tracking as the main contributors and describes feedback as least useful. v2 instead explains gains through hierarchical decomposition, tools and cross-file information, and discusses the limited contribution of retrieval. The external-test-oracle limitation disappears, while coordination overhead, predefined-role generalization and tool-integration delays become explicit limitations. Dependence on backbone capability remains in Section 4.3.

D1.justification: Appendices A.2–A.4 add pseudocode, seven agent prompts and an execution trace with bug metadata. v2 identifies Tavily, SonarQube, GZoltar and the local retrieval corpus, including removal of JavaScript programs, and documents contextual patch matching. The advertised repository changes from Rudra to UniDebugger. Conversely, v1's explicit Python version, top-p and temperature settings are no longer supplied.

R1.justification: v2 grounds its contribution in Hale and Haworth's cognitive debugging model and adds substantial positioning against multi-agent systems such as MetaGPT, ChatDev, AgentCoder and MapCoder. It contrasts cognitive-stage agents with simulated expert teamwork and substantially condenses v1's APR and prompting discussion. This goes beyond citation-format and publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: The title and most of the narrative are rewritten around hierarchical coordination. Standalone Background and Motivation sections disappear, Related Work moves near the beginning, and the research-question-based evaluation is reorganized into experiment subsections. v2 also introduces separate limitations and ethics sections and a structured appendix.

P2.justification: The flat workflow diagram is replaced by a three-level architecture diagram and supplemented with an L3 interaction example. The comparison table gains Defects4J columns and color coding; ablation tables are rebuilt around agent membership, tools and cost. New overlap, prompt and execution-trace figures replace or substantially extend the earlier bug illustrations, alongside a different document layout.

improvement.justification: Defects4J evaluation, agent/tool ablations and explicit prompts address v1's lack of repository-scale evidence and improve inspectability. However, v2 drops ConDefects correctness counts and decoding settings, and its new evidence has material problems: unexplained 286/291 Defects4J totals and an allegedly successful Appendix A.4 patch that still routes 0x80000000 to Integer despite Figure 17 expecting Long. These benefits and weaknesses leave the net quality change uncertain.
